analyses.what_happens:
How the trace is read (consistent with the nnc_fv_s_CHK_002 register and with the env assumptions): each i_clk_rd edge samples the values of the step before it. Read edges are at steps 1,3,5,7,9,11.
- Step 2: i_rst_n_rd=0, a read-only hardware reset, released at the edge at step 3. In the same step i_rst_n_sw=0. The write edge at step 3 takes the software-reset request, so o_sw_rst_busy=1 for steps 3-6 and req_wr=1.
- Read edges 5 and 7: req_wr passes through the read-side 2-FF synchronizer, so w_req_s=1 from step 7.
- Step 7: i_rst_n_wr=0, a write-only hardware reset in the middle of the software-reset sequence. It clears busy and req_wr asynchronously (busy=0 from step 7). The read domain is not reset at this time.
- Step 8: i_rst_n_wr=1, i_rd_en=1, o_empty=1, i_rst_n_sw=1, busy=0. The edge at step 9 matches the antecedent (nnc_fv_s_CHK_002=1 at steps 9-10).
- At that same edge the read side still has w_req_s=1. The read is blocked, so reg_underflow gets 0 and the read FSM goes RUN->RST.
- The edge at step 11 sees o_underflow=0 (step 10), and a_CHK_002 fails.
The env pairing helper lets the read through. The read reset at step 2 and the write reset at step 7 do not overlap, yet the helper counts them as 'both domains reset': w_rst_pend=0 at step 8.
analyses.spec_says:
- contract.json:268 (CHK-002 b): "If i_rd_en=1 and o_empty=1 at edge n, and at that instant i_rst_n_wr=1, i_rst_n_sw=1 and o_sw_rst_busy=0 (no software reset in progress), then o_underflow=1 at edge n+1."
- spec/AsyncGrayFIFO_Design_Specification.md:436: "If only one domain gets a hardware reset during a software reset, the handshake can wait forever for the other domain; the IP does not repair it (ASM-005 applies)."
- spec:1498 (DEC-031), also rules.json:10729 (AF-20.2-27): "A hardware reset of one domain only during the sequence is not repaired (ASM-005 unchanged)."
- spec:1099 (ERR-003): "Reset asserted in one domain only, after the FIFO was used | FIFO state inconsistent; not detected | ... | Reset both domains | Integrator responsibility (ASM-005)".
- spec:1461 (ASM-005): "No FIFO operation (write or read) starts before both domains have left reset."
- contract.json:758 (CHK-023): "The handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked. After both domains are reset, the FIFO works normally."
- spec:154 and 1476: "The two resets are independent and need not be asserted at the same time."
analyses.rtl_does:
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:93: w_rd_blk = w_req_s | (FSM != RUN).
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:154: reg_underflow <= i_rd_en & ~w_rd_blk & w_empty_n, so an underflow is suppressed while the synchronized request is 1.
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:218-227: the req synchronizer is reset only by i_rst_n_rd. It keeps the stale request after the write side is hardware-reset.
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:163-171: the read FSM enters RST/ACK on that stale request.
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:208-221: busy and req_wr are cleared asynchronously by i_rst_n_wr (DEC-031 priority).
This is the documented behavior of a one-domain hardware reset during a software reset (spec:436). It does not by itself show a defect.
analyses.checker_does:
- verif/sva/nnc_chk_rd.sv:62-63 uses only write-domain ports to decide 'no software reset in progress': `(i_rd_en && o_empty && i_rst_n_wr && i_rst_n_sw && !o_sw_rst_busy) |=> o_underflow`. It cannot see that the read side is still blocked by a request that was in flight when the write domain was hardware-reset.
- verif/formal/nnc_env.sv:71-99 (ENV-07/08 pairing): r_wr_hit/r_rd_hit close the window as soon as each domain has been reset at any time. A read reset (step 2) and a later, non-overlapping write reset (step 7) count as 'both reset', so reads are allowed again at step 8.

candidates.evidence_for: The only hardware reset during the software-reset sequence (busy=1, steps 3-6) is the write reset at step 7. The read reset at step 2 came before the request was taken. This is the case spec:436 / DEC-031 (rules.json:10729) / ERR-003 (spec:1099) call unrepaired and an integrator responsibility. CHK-023 (contract.json:758) also says the handshake after a one-domain reset is not checked. The env pairing (nnc_env.sv:75-89) accepts two non-overlapping one-domain resets as a full reset of both domains. Rules not yet assumed: ASM-005 / ERR-003 / DEC-031 (AF-20.1-05, AF-12-07, AF-7.2-12, AF-20.2-27).
candidates.evidence_against: The spec allows the two resets to be asserted at different times (spec:154, 1476: "need not be asserted at the same time"). It never says in words that they must overlap, so the exact form of the assumption needs a designer decision.

candidates.evidence_for: The antecedent's proxy for 'no software reset in progress' (nnc_chk_rd.sv:63) is write-domain only. After a write-only hardware reset during the sequence, busy=0 while the read block (rd.sv:93) is still active. CHK-023 says this handshake is not checked.
candidates.evidence_against: In every legal sequence (no one-domain hardware reset during the handshake), busy falls only after the read FSM has returned to RUN (wr.sv:184-186 waits for !w_ack_s, and the ack drops only when the read FSM leaves ACK, rd.sv:168-170, 186). So the proxy is sound under the spec's reset obligations. The failure needs an out-of-spec reset.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec does not say whether 'reset both domains' (ERR-003 recovery) needs the two reset windows to overlap, or whether a read reset that is released before the write reset starts counts.
candidates.evidence_against: DEC-031 already says a hardware reset of one domain only during the sequence is not repaired. That reading covers this trace without any new spec text.

candidates.evidence_for: o_underflow stays 0 for a read on an empty FIFO while busy=0.
candidates.evidence_against: The RTL does exactly what spec:436 describes for a one-domain hardware reset during a software reset. The read side is blocked by the stale request (rd.sv:93, 154). No spec rule requires the read side to un-block when only the write domain is reset.

analyses.options:
1. E (recommended): tighten the ENV-07/08 pairing helper (nnc_env.sv:71-99) so a one-domain reset is paired only when the two reset windows overlap: the other domain's reset is asserted before this one is released. Equivalently: a one-domain reset that is released while the other domain is running starts a new pending window. Cite ASM-005 / ERR-003 / DEC-031 (spec:436, 1099, 1461, 1498). This also removes the CHK-003 and CHK-013 counterexamples.
2. C: ask the designer to confirm that 'reset both domains' means overlapping reset windows. The spec stimulus already uses overlap (CHK-022/023/024, spec:946).
3. B (only if the designer rejects 1/2): add a checker-side helper that marks the rest of the window 'not checked' after a one-domain hardware reset while busy=1, as CHK-023 (contract.json:758) allows. Do not drop part (b) in general.
4. A: no RTL change is supported by the spec.

analyses.what_happens:
The edge at step N samples the values of step N-1. Read edges are at steps 1,4,6,8,10,12; write edges at 1,3,7,9.
- Write edge 3 (step 2: i_wr_en=1, o_full=0) accepts one word, so wbin=1.
- Step 3: read-only hardware reset (i_rst_n_rd=0), released at step 4. The read domain then synchronizes the un-reset write pointer (wgray=1), so w_wgray_s=1 and o_empty=0 at step 8.
- Steps 7-8: write-only hardware reset (wbin, wgray -> 0). Write reset released at step 9.
- The env pairing closes the window at step 9 (read reset at 3 plus write reset at 7, no overlap), so the read at step 9 is allowed (i_rd_en=1).
- Read edge 10: the read is accepted against the stale w_wgray_s=1, so rbin=1. In the same edge w_wgray_s becomes 0. Occupancy estimate = 0-1 = 15 (4-bit); o_empty stays 0 (rgray=1 != 0).
- i_empty_thr changes 15->11 at step 11. ENV-02 does not constrain it, because i_rst_n_wr was 0 at the previous sample.
- Read edge 12 samples step 11: o_empty=0, o_empty_thr=(15<=11)=0 with i_empty_thr=11 >= 8. Part (b) of a_CHK_003 fails.
With any static threshold from 8 to 14 the same bogus occupancy of 15 would still fail (b). So the threshold change is not the root cause.
analyses.spec_says:
- contract.json:287 (CHK-003 b): "If i_empty_thr >= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_empty_thr=1."
- spec:424 / rules.json:4113 (AF-7.2-12): "If only one domain is reset after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent. The IP neither detects nor repairs this (ASM-005)."
- spec:1099 (ERR-003): recovery is "Reset both domains | Integrator responsibility".
- spec:1461 (ASM-005): "No FIFO operation (write or read) starts before both domains have left reset. Consequence ... if one domain is reset alone after the FIFO was used, the pointer state ... becomes inconsistent and the IP does not detect it."
- spec:154: "The two resets are independent and need not be asserted at the same time."
- rules.json:12923: the occupancy difference is "taken modulo 2 x depth".
- Thresholds: spec:301 says i_empty_thr "shall not change while the FIFO is in use (CDC-004)". The designer decision at rules.json:12788 says "'In use' = from the release of both hardware resets to the end of the test ... not changed while in use".
analyses.rtl_does:
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:112: w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin (modulo 16).
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:118: o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr).
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:97 and 100: a read is accepted when reg_rgray != w_wgray_s.
- rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:206-215: the write-pointer synchronizer is reset only by i_rst_n_rd, so it still holds the pre-reset write pointer after a write-only reset.
The read side accepts a phantom read, rbin passes wbin, and occupancy wraps to 15. This is the 'inconsistent pointer state' that AF-7.2-12 says the IP does not detect or repair. Under consistent pointers (occupancy <= 8) the formula meets (b).

candidates.evidence_for: The read reset at step 3 is a one-domain reset after the FIFO was used (one word written). The write reset at steps 7-8 is a second one-domain reset, after the read domain had already resynchronized the old write pointer. AF-7.2-12 / ASM-005 / ERR-003 make such a state inconsistent and an integrator responsibility. The env helper (nnc_env.sv:75-89) treats the two separate resets as a clean reset of both domains. A second gap: ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:47-49) lets i_empty_thr change after the first release of both resets, which the designer decision (rules.json:12788) forbids until the end of the test.
candidates.evidence_against: The spec says the resets need not be asserted together (spec:154, 1476). It does not say in words that they must overlap, so the pairing rule needs designer confirmation.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec does not say whether the ERR-003 recovery 'reset both domains' needs overlapping reset windows. Two disjoint one-domain resets are not explicitly excluded.
candidates.evidence_against: All spec reset scenarios use overlapping resets (CHK-022 contract.json:739, CHK-023 :757, CHK-024 :770; spec:946). Each disjoint reset is itself 'one domain reset alone after the FIFO was used' (spec:1461).

candidates.evidence_for: o_empty_thr=0 with i_empty_thr=11 >= depth, and a read was accepted when the write pointer had already been reset to 0.
candidates.evidence_against: The DUT computes occupancy modulo 2*depth, as the spec answer requires (rules.json:12923). The wrap to 15 comes only from the inconsistent pointer state that the spec says is not repaired (AF-7.2-12). Under ASM-005-compliant resets the occupancy stays within 0..8.

analyses.options:
1. E (recommended): change the ENV-07/08 pairing (nnc_env.sv:71-99) so a pair of hardware resets closes the pending window only if the two reset windows overlap. A one-domain reset that is released while the other domain runs keeps or opens the pending state, so no access happens until a real reset of both domains. Rule: ASM-005 / ERR-003 / AF-7.2-12 (spec:424, 1099, 1461).
2. E (secondary): strengthen ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:47-49) to keep i_empty_thr stable from the first release of both resets onward, not only while both are high. Rule: AF-3-17 / AF-7.2-04 and the decision at rules.json:12788. This alone does not remove this counterexample.
3. C: have the designer confirm that the 'reset both domains' recovery means overlapping resets.
4. A or B: no change is supported by the spec.

analyses.what_happens:
Read edges are at steps 1,4,6,8; cap_* are captured at negedges (steps 2,5,7).
- i_rst_n_wr=0 from step 4 on. The read domain stays out of reset until step 8.
- Step 6 (read edge): o_empty=0 and o_empty_thr=0; the negedge at step 7 captures cap_empty_thr=0.
- Step 7: i_empty_thr changes 0->7 between read edges. The combinational o_empty_thr becomes (occ=1 <= 7)=1.
- The edge at step 8 samples step 7: o_empty_thr=1 != cap_empty_thr=0, so a_CHK_004 fails.
No other read output changed: o_empty == cap_empty, and o_rd_data == cap_rd_data (0x20010077). ENV-02 does not constrain i_empty_thr at this time, because i_rst_n_wr=0.
analyses.spec_says:
- contract.json:301 (CHK-004): "o_empty, o_empty_thr and o_underflow change value only in the time step of a rising edge of i_clk_rd or of an assertion of i_rst_n_rd."
- rules.json:2880 (AF-6.2-06, LVL-STS): "It changes after a clock edge (or after a synchronizer stage), never between edges except for the effect of the static thresholds."
- spec:304 / rules.json:3240 (AF-6.2-21): o_empty_thr is a "Combinational function of i_empty_thr and the pointers".
- spec:301: i_empty_thr "shall not change while the FIFO is in use (CDC-004)".
- spec:418 / rules.json:3963 (AF-7.2-04): "static: written once before the FIFO is used and not changed while it is in use (DEC-017)".
- Designer decision, rules.json:12788: "'In use' = from the release of both hardware resets to the end of the test. The thresholds are set before the resets are released and are not changed while in use ... Changing them in use is outside the specification". The same decision is repeated at rules.json:12827.
analyses.rtl_does: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:118: o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1'b1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr). This is a combinational path from i_empty_thr, as the spec specifies (spec:304). The output changes in the same step as the threshold input.
analyses.checker_does:
- verif/sva/nnc_chk_rd.sv:47-53 captures o_empty_thr at negedge i_clk_rd.
- verif/sva/nnc_chk_rd.sv:81-83 requires o_empty_thr == cap_empty_thr at the next posedge. It has no exception for a change of i_empty_thr.
- By contrast, the write-side counterpart CHK-012 does exempt a threshold change: verif/sva/nnc_chk_wr.sv:56 (`cap_fthr <= i_full_thr; // or of the static threshold (AF-6.2-06)`) and line 117.
- verif/formal/nnc_env.sv:47-49 (ENV-02) assumes $stable(i_empty_thr) only when i_rst_n_rd and i_rst_n_wr are 1 now and at the previous read edge. So the threshold is free while either domain is in reset, even long after the first release.

candidates.evidence_for: Both resets were released at step 1, so by the designer decision (rules.json:12788) the FIFO is 'in use' to the end of the test, and i_empty_thr must not change. The change at step 7 is 'outside the specification'. ENV-02 (nnc_env.sv:47-49) is weaker than this decision: it frees the threshold whenever either domain is in reset. Rule: AF-3-17 / AF-7.2-04 / CDC-004 (spec:301, 418) with the decision at rules.json:12788.
candidates.evidence_against: The decision's wording ('from the release of both hardware resets') could be read as restarting at every later reset release. Under that reading a change during a later write-only reset would not be covered.

candidates.evidence_for: AF-6.2-06 (rules.json:2880) explicitly allows a status level to change between edges for 'the effect of the static thresholds', and CHK-012 already has this exception (nnc_chk_wr.sv:56, 117). CHK-004 (nnc_chk_rd.sv:81-83) does not mirror it for o_empty_thr.
candidates.evidence_against: The CHK-004 behavior text (contract.json:301) lists no threshold exception, and with a spec-compliant environment the threshold never changes. So the exception would only matter for out-of-spec stimulus.
The spec requires o_empty_thr to be a combinational function of i_empty_thr (spec:304, rules.json:3240), and AF-6.2-06 allows exactly this effect. The RTL (rd.sv:118) follows the spec.

Once both hardware resets have been released for the first time, i_empty_thr stays stable at every read edge to the end of the trace, whatever later reset activity occurs. Make the same change to ENV-01 for i_full_thr (lines 41-44).
2. B (alternative, spec-backed by AF-6.2-06): add a captured i_empty_thr to nnc_chk_rd.sv (like cap_fthr in nnc_chk_wr.sv:56). Exempt o_empty_thr (not o_rd_data, o_empty or o_underflow) when i_empty_thr changed since the negedge capture.

analyses.what_happens:
Write edges are at steps 1,3,5,9,11,13,15; read edges at 1,4,6,8,10,12. Each edge samples the previous step.
- Write edge 3 accepts one word (step 2: i_wr_en=1, o_full=0), so wbin=1.
- Step 3: read-only reset, released at step 4. The read synchronizer picks up wgray=1, so o_empty=0 at step 8.
- Step 8: write-only reset (wbin=0), released at step 9. The env pairing closes the window at step 9, so the read at step 9 is allowed.
- Read edge 10: the read is accepted against the stale w_wgray_s, so rbin=1, rgray=1.
- Step 11: read-only reset again (rbin=0). Before it, write edge 11 had already captured rgray=1 into the read-pointer synchronizer, and write edge 13 moves it to the output: w_rgray_s=1 while wbin=0. The write-domain occupancy is 0-1 = 15.
- Step 13: i_rst_n_sw=0, so the flags are blocked.
- Step 14: i_rst_n_sw=1, busy=0, o_full=0, and i_full_thr changes 0->9. ENV-01 does not constrain it, because i_rst_n_rd=0. Then o_full_thr=(15>=9)=1.
- Write edge 15 samples step 14: i_full_thr=9 > 8 with o_full_thr=1. Part (b) of a_CHK_013 fails.
With a static i_full_thr=8 the check would still fail in part (c) (o_full_thr=1 but o_full=0), so the root cause is the inconsistent pointers. i_full_thr also changes at steps 2, 3, 4, 10 and 14 after the first release of both resets.
analyses.spec_says:
- contract.json:524 (CHK-013 b): "if i_full_thr > PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH (9..15), then o_full_thr=0".
- rules.json:12923: "a value above the depth makes it never 1". The difference is taken "modulo 2 x depth".
- spec:424 / rules.json:4113 (AF-7.2-12): "If only one domain is reset after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent. The IP neither detects nor repairs this (ASM-005)."
- spec:1099 (ERR-003): recovery is "Reset both domains | Integrator responsibility".
- spec:1461 (ASM-005): no operation before both domains have left reset; a one-domain reset after use gives an inconsistent state.
- Thresholds: spec:287 says i_full_thr "shall not change while the FIFO is in use (CDC-004)". The decision at rules.json:12788 sets 'in use' to run "from the release of both hardware resets to the end of the test".
